data.long_meaning: The name Fakhry is derived from the Arabic root word 'fakhara', which means to rejoice or be joyful. In Islamic history, the name Fakhry has been given to many prominent figures who have brought joy and triumph to their communities. For instance, Fakhry Al-Din Mahmud Shah was a sultan of the Bengal Sultanate who ruled from 1338 to 1340 and is remembered for his military victories and prosperous rule. The name Fakhry is also mentioned in the Quran as a name of Allah, which means the Subduer or the Conqueror.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine triumph and joy
data.etymology: Fakhry belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joy, Delight, Triumph.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fakhry total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Caliph Al-Fakhry I bin Al-Qadir, the Almohad Caliph (1121-1160 AD) who expanded the Almohad Empire from Morocco to Spain.
historical_references.context: Al-Fakhry I, whose real name was Abu Muhammad Abd al-Mu'min, was the third Almohad Caliph. He succeeded his father, Ali ibn Yusuf I, in 1121 AD. Under his rule, the Almohad Empire saw a period of expansion, reaching its greatest territorial extent. Al-Fakhry I is also remembered for his military campaigns against the Almoravids and the Christian Reconquistadors.

historical_references.reference: Sultan Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah Bahmani (1358-1389 AD), the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate in India.
historical_references.context: Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah was a Sultan of the Tughlaq Empire in India. In 1351 AD, he rebelled against the Tughlaq Sultan Firuz Shah. After a long struggle, he established the Bahmani Sultanate in 1347 AD. The Bahmani Sultanate became one of the major powers in India, ruling over parts of the Deccan region. Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah is considered the founder of the Bahmani Dynasty, which ruled until 1518 AD.
